content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xsd 1.1 features within XML Schema Definition (XSD). You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XSD 1.1 Features matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about assertions, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: An XML Schema (XSD) defines a vocabulary contract: element and attribute declarations, types, cardinality, ordering, and constraints. A document can be well-formed yet fail schema validation because its data does not conform to the contract.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Assertions; Conditional type assignment; New validation capabilities; Differences from XSD 1.0; Checking processor support before use. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XSD 1.1 Features
content_blocks.expected_output: Use this schema to validate a separate instance document such as <price>19.95</price>; a validating XSD processor rejects non-decimal text for this declared type. XSD 1.1-only features require a supporting processor.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Keep schema namespaces and targetNamespace choices consistent; validate representative valid and invalid instances. XSD 1.1 assertions and conditional type assignment are specification features but are not available in every validator.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is an inspectable example, not an XML execution service. Validate it with a standards-compatible XML processor; feature support depends on the processor/version.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Assertions”. Then add one boundary case involving “Conditional type assignment”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
